content.title: About
content.content: Palak Paneer is a classic Indian dish consisting of soft cottage cheese (paneer) cooked with spinach (palak) in a fragrant blend of spices. The dish is rich in protein, calcium, and iron, offering a creamy taste with a mild earthy note from the spinach.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Palak Paneer is often served in Indian restaurants as a vegetarian alternative to meat dishes.
Traditionally, paneer is made from whole milk without rennet, making it suitable for vegetarians.
Spinach used in the dish is high in iron, and its absorption is enhanced by vitamin C present in the spices.
Typical recipes include tomato puree, ginger, garlic, and garam masala, giving the dish its characteristic aroma.
In some regions, toasted cashews are added for extra richness.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Paneer provides high‑quality plant‑based protein important for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium for bone health
items.content: The cheese contributes a significant amount of calcium, supporting bone density.

items.title: Iron and energy
items.content: Spinach supplies iron, which is essential for oxygen transport and energy production.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamin B6 and folate, which aid metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Spices such as turmeric and cumin have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Paneer is made from milk, so people with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: When salt and soy sauce are added, the dish can become high in sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Spinach contains oxalates that can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy should avoid paneer.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Palak Paneer is served hot, typically with basmati rice, naan, or chapati. It can be rolled in flatbreads, used as a filling for wraps, or enjoyed as a standalone main course. Garnish with fresh cilantro or toasted cashews for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked Palak Paneer in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.
